entities.name: Query Env gp160
observations: 768 aa viral envelope precursor with GP120 domains at residues 33–509 and GP41 domain at residues 528–717 by Pfam.
Shows strong homology to curated HIV-1 group M Env gp160 proteins: 74.8–75.5% identity and 100% query coverage.
Architecture is consistent with an N-terminal signal peptide, large glycosylated exterior subunit, furin-processing region, fusion subunit, transmembrane anchor, and cytoplasmic tail.
Likely forms a trimeric envelope spike and is processed into gp120 and gp41; these are homology-based functional inferences, not direct experiments on this sequence.
Likely localizes to the viral envelope and host-cell secretory/plasma or endosomal membranes as a single-pass type I membrane glycoprotein.
Likely biological roles include host-cell attachment, receptor/coreceptor engagement, and class I membrane fusion during viral entry.

entities.name: HIV-1 Env gp160
observations: Curated HIV-1 Env gp160 references describe furin-like cleavage into gp120 and gp41, trimeric spike assembly, CD4/coreceptor-mediated attachment, and class I viral membrane fusion.
Curated localization includes virion membrane, host-cell membrane, host endosome membrane, and single-pass type I membrane topology.

entities.name: HIV entry and fusion
observations: The homologous Env proteins participate in virion attachment, clathrin-dependent uptake, and fusion of viral and host membranes; exact pathway assignment for the query is inferred from homology.
